answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and publish its past deals on a shared ledger. A juniper seller with a long record keeps its deposit and earns repeat work, while a cedar newcomer starts with small orders until it builds the same history. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits plus the time to fake a history, which turns the old fable of free identities into an expensive job. Cheating loses the deposit, so one real identity beats many cheap ones.
